posts.name: Amnachaidh
posts.cooked:
From the Sentinels Tactics thread (not a cut, just stealing the disussion topic idea) -- who was the first hero you played in SotM, and what impression did it give you?

My first game was - rather unwisely - as Absolute Zero. I saw how things could come together at a very low level, and we won on the strength of the other players. It was first edition, so there was no "H" mechanic, so my dead weight didn't gravely cost the team. I didn't get the full awesome of AZ, but I also saw that Wraith, Haka, Ra and Legacy were able to stomp the Baron into the ground.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
My first was a two player game with two heroes (like many people, I missed the section of the rules that says this isn't a good idea). I played Tempest because he looked cool, and I think my boyfriend played Ra. 

We saved Insula Primalis from the ravages of Baron Blade. Yay!

Now I've told this story multiple times now but I was really expecting not to like it at all, being a person who doesn't like comic books or superheroes and predominantly plays Eurogames. A couple of turns in and I was completely hooked - there are enough decisions and the idea of working out the effects of my different options and assessing which is the best for this particular situation was very appealing to my Eurogamer side, and getting to smash someone's face in mercilessly appeals to pretty much everyone, right?

It just goes to show that sometimes my first impressions are utterly, completely wrong.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
I played Bunker alongside Ra, Legacy, Tempest, and (most importantly to this story) Tachyon in an epic battle to keep Voss from invading Megalopolis.  During that game, Tachyon (played by my sister) and I developed a great running gag of her saying something interested or curious about some of Voss' mad science, and me yelling at her ("Oooh, I see, the clamps along the back of the skull must allow for remote control - but wouldn't that arrangement result in limited range?" "I'm just glad the range is still long enough he can't hear you telling him how to improve his minions!").  It was a great first game, with a couple of tense turns where it looked like we might get overwhelmed, then a quick board clearing, an Egyptian god blowing up a space ship, and Tempest frying his nemesis.

It was about two games later that I realized Bunker is effectively unplayable, beginning my longstanding love-hate relationship with that deck, and my interest in proxies and variants for it.

posts.name: mlangsdorf
posts.cooked:
I played Legacy in a 5 player game with some friends playing the other complexity 1 heroes (Ra, Haka, Wraith, and Bunker) against Omnitron in Megaopolis. I really like Legacy, as I liked being a buff character and everyone appreciated the bonus damage. I didn't under Legacy's deck very well at first, and couldn't realize why I would play cards like Heroic Intercept or Lead from the Front. I never saw Next Evolution nor the Legacy Ring until I played a couple more time.

I remeber that my friend with was playing the Wraith got out a Utility Belt early on and thought the character was just awesome, since she could use Throwing Knives and Stealth every turn.

I played Legacy first, because we just grabbed level 1's without looking at their mechanics. I actually enjoy playing as a party buff type character, so I enjoyed myself a lot. 

We got a fair bit wrong in that game, because we misread, or outright missed parts of the rules and gameplay, but we managed to figure it out by our second game, which I played as my favourite Glass Cannon, Absolute Zero.

I mention this, because both showed me how fun the game can be, but also just how much bookkeeping can be required.

posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked:
I played Chrono Ranger first. I was at a board game night with my improv group the week before thanksgiving and the girl sitting next to me had sentinels sitting on the seat. And I loved the art and the theme. So about 2 hours in we were looking for a new game and I asked if we could play that one. We did and I fell in love.

Now on talking about my feelings for the space time cowboy. The girl who owned it said he was a set up heavy hero but once I got going I flew through his cards. There were several rule problems with that game, namely backlash field only going off once a round and not counting Bounties in the card that hurts you for the number of cards in play.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
My first hero was Mr. Fixer, and I loved it. The game was Fixer, Ra, Tempest vs Plague Rat... I think in Rook City. Some friends of mine had just gotten Rook City and introduced me to the game. I got dual crowbars, some style (I think grease monkey), and harmony and just laid a beatdown on the rat for most of the game (I think we were misreading crowbars and allowing me to hit the same target twice). I felt awesome, even if I wasn't able to change things up much, but building a 1 point hit into a 8 pt hit every turn was so much fun.

 

This game was also were I first saw Ra burn himself to a crisp with Flame Shield, and I went down not long after, leaving Tempest with the Cleansing Downpour barely hangning on long enough to pull a lightning slash and a victory.

 

Loved the game enough that I eventually scoured the webs and my bank to buy "all the things" and now play solo (stupid work schedule)

posts.name: Under3
posts.cooked:
As I have mentioned my first hero was Absolute Zero, as soon as I opened the box and had a quick look at the decks he was the one who instantly leapt out at me as the one I really wanted to try first; everything about him just seemed more interesting at first glance than the others both visually/thematically and in gameplay with the clear damage redirection and strange base power.
The game was with one other friend, and I can't remember who else was played, against Baron Blade in Megalopolis (even though thematically Omnitron was my favourite villain from the base game but the high hit points and potential to hang around made me wary to try for the first game). I didn't find him too tricky, I was perhaps lucky to get through some decent card draws, and setting off his damage rebounding combos was great fun, he is still easily my favourite to play when he goes well.

After that I tried playing as him against Omnitron on Wagner Mars Base and realised the utter pain of how badly his deck can be shut down with what felt like constant red dust and technological singularities.
But I still love the guy.
